newsitem.title: UK: NatWest seen weak after in-line results.
newsitem.headline: NatWest seen weak after in-line results.

text.p: Shares in National Westminster Bank Plc were seen opening weak on Tuesday after the banking group's first-half profits provided few positive surprises, dealers said.
"The initial reaction will probably be to call them lower," said one senior dealer, "but the comment from analysts will probably be to the effect that we have seen the worst."

Dogged in recent months by losses in derivatives trading at its NatWest Markets unit, the stock has underperformed rivals in the sector which have focused more on expanding their domestic retail operations.
Yet dealers noted that NatWest has already detailed a reorganisation of its investment banking operations and today's statement added little to its previous announcements.
NatWest said pre-tax profit on continuing operations, excluding a charge of 106 million stg, rose 17 percent to 775 million stg from 662 million a year before.
Analyst forecasts had been mostly in a range between 757 million stg and 770 million.
The interim dividend was raised 10.4 percent to 10.6p, matching forecasts.

In line with its previous statements, NatWest said its treasury business would become a separate sector while its NatWest Markets unit would be "taken forward under new leadership on a clearly focused basis with close regard to profitability."
In retail and commercial banking, NatWest said it was imperative that it significantly cuts costs and makes better use of existing customer relationships.
